title: Signal Bridge — Model Compatibility Catalog & Procurement Prioritizer
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: procurement and platform teams routinely make ad-hoc choices when a model becomes attractive (price drop, new quantization, vendor SLA). We lack a normalized, machine-readable surface that maps external signals (model size, quantization formats, licensing, release cadence) to an operational compatibility score and a procurement priority. This creates friction: inaccurate switch-cost estimates, missed fallback candidates, and slow decision cycles for Dedicated/Private customers.

Proposed solution: build 'Signal Bridge' — an internal catalog and scoring service that ingests disparate model landscape signals and emits two primary artifacts: (1) a Model Compatibility Record (MCR) with normalized properties and a compatibility_score, and (2) a Procurement Prioritizer card with switch_cost_estimate, latency_tail_risk, and recommended rollout cadence. The service will power a console dashboard (catalog view + compare mode), procurement runbooks, and periodic alerts for models with high opportunity or risk.

Scope (MVP):
- Ingest pipelines for vendor release notes, GitHub tags, public model manifests, and our nightly benchmark runner outputs.
- Schema for Model Compatibility Record (flat attributes: model_id, architecture, effective_token_cost, quant_formats_supported, last_release_date, vendor_sla_level, known_incompatibilities).
- Compatibility scoring algorithm (weights configurable via Console).
- Console catalog page: list + compare + quick-prioritizer.
- Exportable procurement card (PDF/JSON) for contract & capacity planning.

Non-goals (MVP): full automated procurement approval, legal contract negotiation integration, or real-time traffic routing changes.

Why this matters: reduces decision latency for switching/fallbacks, standardizes model-fit conversations between PM/Procurement/Runtime, and gives predictable input to Dedicated capacity planning and reserved GPU commitments.
metrics: compatibility_score = weighted_sum(quant_readiness: 30%, kernel_availability: 25%, license_compat: 20%, release_cadence: 15%, community_signal: 10%)
milestones: M2 - scoring engine + config UI (2026-03-15 to 2026-03-28)
M3 - console catalog + compare UX (2026-03-29 to 2026-04-08)
M4 - procurement export + stakeholder walkthrough (2026-04-09 to 2026-04-10)
acceptance_criteria: A1: Ingestion pipeline pulls at least 80% of listed public model manifests nightly and records schema-complete MCRs.
A2: Compatibility score computed and surfaced for 200 models with sampling from different vendors.
A3: Console catalog page shows compare mode with side-by-side Procurement Prioritizer cards and export button.
A4: Procurement team signs off on switch_cost_estimate methodology and sample cards for three enterprise scenarios.
risks: Telemetry schema mismatch: nightly_benchmarks needs a column we don't have (ENG-18822) — blocking M1 until resolved.
Signal noise: scraped release notes sometimes omit quantization details — we need fallback heuristics and provenance trace.
Legal/licensing ambiguity could spike procurement effort; ensure procurement/legal review for high-impact vendors.
Overfitting weights: scoring config needs a holdout validation set and periodic recalibration.
implementation_notes: Prefer lightweight Airflow DAG for initial ingestion; switch to event-driven in next quarter.
Store MCRs in existing product-data-store (schema v2) with model_id as primary key.
Expose scoring as an internal HTTP endpoint for other services (runtime & alerts).
